<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24__p008">
  <section v="21">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Everything a person sees or hears is a lesson in divine service, and even apparent chance events are part of Divine Providence, teaching that all details in Torah are instructive.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">And 4)</t>
    <t s="2">Now, the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov is known,</t>
    <t s="3">that everything a person sees or hears is a lesson in the service of G-d.</t>
    <t s="4">And the Maggid adds</t>
    <t s="5">that everything a person sees and hears, and every occurrence that happens to a person, is for the sake of the service of G-d.</t>
    <t s="6">And the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="7">that even every occurrence is by particular Divine Providence,</t>
    <t s="8">and that which is called by the name "chance" is that below, in this world, it is in a manner of chance.</t>
    <t s="9">And analogous to what is written,</t>
    <t s="10">"If a bird's nest chance to be before you," and our Sages said,</t>
    <t s="11">"excluding a prepared one,"</t>
    <t s="12">that even though all matters are by particular Divine Providence,</t>
    <t s="13">and moreover they are prepared from the prior thought of Adam Kadmon,</t>
    <t s="14">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="15">the verse says "if a bird's nest chance to be before you," excluding a prepared one,</t>
    <t s="16">for there are matters whose intention is fulfilled when even below they are in a manner of "prepared,"</t>
    <t s="17">and there are matters whose intention is fulfilled when below they are in a manner of "chance,"</t>
    <t s="18">"if it chance."</t>
    <t s="19">And from this it is understood, all the more so, regarding the matters in Torah,</t>
    <t s="20">that all its details,</t>
    <t s="21">even when they appear externally to be only incidental</t>
    <t s="22">(in the manner of chance),</t>
    <t s="23">they are instructive.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="22">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The attribute of a fortiori (kal vachomer) among the thirteen Torah attributes drawn from the thirteen attributes of mercy in prayer teaches that the drawing down through Torah has a superiority over that through prayer.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that this—that the attribute of the thirteen attributes of Torah which is drawn from the thirteen attributes of mercy in prayer is the attribute of kal vachomer—is to teach,</t>
    <t s="2">that even though the main drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy is in prayer, and through this the drawing down also comes in Torah,</t>
    <t s="3">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="4">there is an advantage in the drawing down that is in Torah relative to the drawing down that is in prayer,</t>
    <t s="5">in the manner of the attribute of kal vachomer,</t>
    <t s="6">for even though the stringent is learned from the lenient,</t>
    <t s="7">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="8">it is stringent relative to the lenient.</t>
    <t s="9">And as is explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="10">that this—that we learn the drawing down that is beyond the measure of the elevation through Torah of many from the drawing down through the prayer of many—is a study in the manner of "all the more so,"</t>
    <t s="11">kal vachomer.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="23">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The difference between Torah and prayer is like the difference between blessing and prayer, where in Torah one becomes a master over the Torah and its flow of influences.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the matter is,</t>
    <t s="1">that the difference between Torah and prayer is analogous to the difference between blessing and prayer.</t>
    <t s="2">For in prayer,</t>
    <t s="3">the one praying is below and asks that they bestow upon him from above,</t>
    <t s="4">and in blessing,</t>
    <t s="5">the one who blesses</t>
    <t s="6">[he who has the power to bless,</t>
    <t s="7">like the kohanim who were given the power to bless]</t>
    <t s="8">is above the source from which the blessing is drawn, and commands that the drawing down be to below.</t>
    <t s="9">And as the language in the Priestly Blessing, "May the L-rd bless you,"</t>
    <t s="10">which is a language of command.</t>
    <t s="11">And likewise is it regarding the drawing down of influences through Torah.</t>
    <t s="12">For since the crown of Torah is ownerless to all,</t>
    <t s="13">behold, it is within the capacity of every single Jew to merit it through engagement in Torah, in a manner that it becomes his Torah</t>
    <t s="14">(of the learner),</t>
    <t s="15">and he becomes a master, as it were, over the Torah, and all the more so over the drawing down of influences through Torah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
